questions.enonce_markdown:
5. (a) Match the following problems in column **ONE** with the corresponding solution that is appropriate in column **TWO**.

| | Problems | | Solutions |
|---|---|---|---|
| i | Disused factory buildings | A | Encouraging the informal sector |
| ii | Water supply shortage | B | Development of business parks |
| iii | Pollution of the air | C | Building of more new roads |
| iv | Unemployment | D | Building more new reservoirs |
| v | Traffic congestion | E | Improve security and discourage rural-urban migration |
| vi | Crime and Vandalism | F | Education and fines for more than allowed emission |

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Problem | Matching solution | Why |
|---|---|---|
| i Disused factory buildings | **B** Development of business parks | old factories are cleared or re-used as business parks and offices, which brings the land back into use |
| ii Water supply shortage | **D** Building more new reservoirs | reservoirs store more water for the growing population |
| iii Pollution of the air | **F** Education and fines for more than allowed emission | people and firms are taught to reduce smoke and fumes and are fined when they exceed the limit |
| iv Unemployment | **A** Encouraging the informal sector | small trades and businesses give work and income to people without formal jobs |
| v Traffic congestion | **C** Building of more new roads | new roads and bypasses give more space and reduce traffic jams |
| vi Crime and Vandalism | **E** Improve security and discourage rural-urban migration | more police and lighting, and fewer people crowding the towns |

**Answer: i-B, ii-D, iii-F, iv-A, v-C, vi-E** (1 mark each).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Briefly describe **TWO** ways by which industrial growth brings about global warming.

(5 marks)

(ii) Study the table and answer the questions that follow:

| Age (Years) | Country A | Country B |
|---|---|---|
| 0-15 | 58% | 15% |
| 16-64 | 38% | 63% |
| 65+ | 4% | 22% |

Which of these is an Advanced Industrialized Country (AIC)? Give **TWO** reasons.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two ways industrial growth causes global warming (5 marks).**

1. **Burning of fossil fuels.** Factories and the power stations that supply them burn coal, oil and gas, which release large amounts of **carbon dioxide** (and other gases such as nitrogen oxides). These **greenhouse gases** trap the heat that the earth sends back to space, so the lower atmosphere becomes warmer (the enhanced greenhouse effect). Industrial growth means more fuel burned each year, and more vehicles carry goods and workers.
2. **Release of other greenhouse gases and clearing of forests.** Some industries release **methane**, **nitrous oxide** and **CFCs/HFCs** (refrigerators, air conditioners, aerosols), which trap heat far more strongly than carbon dioxide; and forests are cleared to provide land, timber and raw materials for industry and housing, which removes the trees that absorb carbon dioxide.

(Two ways, each described: 2.5 marks each.)

**(ii) The Advanced Industrialised Country (5 marks).** The AIC is **Country B**.

*Reasons (2 x 2 marks, with 1 mark for the answer):*

1. **Very few children and a low birth rate:** only **15%** of the people in Country B are aged 0-15, against 58% in Country A. Families are small, because of family planning, women working, the cost of raising children and a high standard of living.
2. **Many old people and a high life expectancy:** **22%** of Country B's people are 65 and over, against 4% in Country A. It shows very good health care, nutrition, housing and pensions, which are features of advanced industrialised countries.
3. **A large working-age group and a low dependency ratio:** **63%** are aged 16-64. The dependency ratio (young + old compared with the workers) is $(15+22)/63 \approx 0.59$ for Country B, against $(58+4)/38 \approx 1.63$ for Country A, which shows that Country B has a strong labour force and an economy that can support its people.

In contrast, **Country A** has a very large young population (58% under 16), a high birth rate, few elderly people and a short life expectancy: a developing country (an LIC).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Outline **TWO** problems and **TWO** solutions of road transport development in Least Industrialized Countries (LICs).

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Two problems (2 marks).**

1. **High cost of construction and maintenance:** roads are expensive to build across forests, swamps, rivers and mountains, and LICs have little capital, so many roads are built slowly and are poorly maintained; potholes and washouts follow.
2. **Poor quality and bad weather:** many roads are not tarred, are narrow and have poor drainage, so they become impassable in the rainy season, causing accidents and delays and isolating villages; heavy loads and poor planning damage them quickly.

**Two solutions (2 marks).**

1. **Raising money:** loans and grants from the World Bank and other donors, public-private partnerships and tolls, and a **road maintenance fund** financed by fuel taxes and road-user charges.
2. **Better planning and techniques:** using **local materials and labour** to cut costs, choosing and tarring the main roads that link production areas to towns and ports, improving drainage, and controlling axle loads and repairing roads regularly.
